# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 85 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 85 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_085_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 2

**1** Now the twelve virgins were carrying the stones and passing them through the gate and giving them to the young men, and the young men were fitting them into the tower. **2** The ones who were not the virgins were dragging stones up from the deep and carrying them. And the deep was on the left side of the gate where the virgins were standing. **3** After all the stones were fitted in, others were taken out of the deep. **4** These stones were brought out all round and fitted into the tower. They were indeed quite smooth around the sides, fitting exactly with the other stones. **5** They were fitted in so well that their joints were not visible; and the tower appeared to be built of a single stone. **6** But other stones were brought up from the deep; some of them were speckled, some rough, some white, and some variegated. And all these were fitted in by the young men. But many of these were carried away and thrown to one side, and many were thrown far from the tower by the virgins themselves, and they lay by the road. **7** But others that had been removed by them, the stone-workers applied to the stone from the deep from which they had been cut; and they were not fitted in, for they were found to be useless for the building. **8** And he said to me, "Do you see these stones?" "I see them, Lord," I said. "These stones that are thrown away," he said, "will never enter the tower." **9** Some of the stones lying by the road were broken in two; some were cracked; some were chipped all around; some were completely shattered; and some remained whole. But most of them remained whole for that place.

---

*EMET renders building terminology precisely. "The deep" (abyssos) is the water from which the stones are drawn — baptism. The stones from the deep that do not fit the tower represent those who have received baptism but are not incorporated into the Church due to sin.*
